subject: PD brief 26 Oct – 2 Nov 2026: 51 papers, 3 to dig into

synthesis.intro: These 8 days were dominated by cardiac arrest research — bystander CPR, post-ROSC care, ventilation quality and prehospital blood in trauma also featured — alongside a cluster of workforce wellbeing and operations papers.
synthesis.discussion: If real-time ventilation feedback lifted in-target ventilations from 7.5% to 39.0% in arrests, what is the equivalent gap in your own arrest routine that technology or a crew agreement could close?

lessons.text: Real-time BVM feedback saw ventilations hitting both rate and volume targets jump from 7.5% to 39.0%, while ETCO2 monitoring alone caught almost none of the low-tidal-volume ventilations. On your next arrest, consider what feedback your setup actually gives you beyond a waveform.

Women still receive bystander CPR less often than men in public, in both North Carolina (44% vs 48%) and Singapore (52% vs 59%). A reminder to coach any hesitant bystander early and specifically on public arrest calls.

In a large prospective evaluation, no patient survived resuscitative thoracotomy beyond 10 minutes of traumatic cardiac arrest, though outcomes with tamponade were far better than exsanguination. This suggests scene-time judgement before transport matters as much as the intervention itself.

Nursing-home arrests were far more often shockable than home arrests (36.3% vs 7.1%), yet survival was worst there. Consider whether your mental model of an arrest in an aged-care facility matches the rhythm you are likely to find.

A trauma systematic review found all four common analgesic classes effective with essentially no drug-attributed serious adverse events across 17,115 patients. If you have been hesitant about ketamine or methoxyflurane in injured patients, this supports the current approach.

deep_dives.why: What happens in the minutes after ROSC drives outcomes, and this period brought several papers on predicting rearrest, recovery and ACS — all still hypothesis-generating but directly relevant to transport and destination decisions.
questions: Which post-ROSC patients you transport would you flag as high rearrest risk, and what would you do differently en route?
The rearrest prediction worked best only one minute out — is there any realistic way to act on a prediction that close to the event?
If a model could reliably exclude ACS on the post-ROSC ECG, how would that change your destination conversations?
deep_dives.ideas: Compare the predictors across the three papers — rhythm, age, collapse duration, PaCO2 — and consider which are already visible to you on scene. Look at how each paper defines a good outcome and ask whether that matches what your receiving services promise families.

deep_dives.why: Three trauma papers this period point the same direction: earlier recognition of bleeding and closer attention to what prehospital blood products do to the patient before arrival.
questions: Would a narrowed pulse pressure change your trauma assessment in a patient whose SBP still looks acceptable?
How confident are you that your undertriage rate for older trauma patients is better than the 53% reported here?
Does your local practice monitor calcium in patients receiving prehospital blood?
deep_dives.ideas: Compare the pulse pressure cut-off against how your local guideline defines shock, and consider where it sits for your older patients on beta-blockers. Ask whether your trauma triage tool would have caught the undertriaged patients described here.

deep_dives.why: Bystanders carry a heavy emotional load after doing CPR, and a separate paper proposes supportive follow-up for those on unsuccessful resuscitations — both touch on how we hand back to the public after an arrest.
questions: When you leave the scene of an arrest, what does the bystander who did compressions actually get from you?
How would you respond if a bystander asked you directly whether the person survived?
Does your service have a pathway for following up bystanders, and would you know how to refer one?
deep_dives.ideas: Compare the four themes from the interviewed bystanders with your own last arrest scene handover. Consider whether the proposed supportive follow-up model could fit the referral pathways available in your area.

papers.title: Prehospital pulse pressure flags trauma bleeding
papers.design: Retrospective multicentre cohort
papers.n: 2,177 adult trauma patients (68 with active haemorrhage)
papers.finding: Prehospital pulse pressure predicted active haemorrhage (AUC 0.73, similar to SBP 0.74); each 10 mmHg narrowing raised the odds by 51% (OR 1.51, 95% CI 1.28–1.79), and PP ≤45 mmHg was best for rule-out given high negative predictive value

papers.title: ECPR timing in refractory OHCA: survival gap persists
papers.journal: European Heart Journal. Acute Cardiovascular Care
papers.design: Nationwide registry target trial emulation (sequential landmark)
papers.n: 58,668 patients with refractory OHCA (909 received ECPR)
papers.finding: Weighted 30-day survival with ECPR vs conventional CPR was 31.0% vs 16.0%, 21.6% vs 7.2% and 10.9% vs 3.2% at 15, 30 and 60 minutes after ED arrival; an exploratory analysis found benefit narrowed but stayed significant to 120 minutes

papers.title: Instrumented manikin neck for immobilisation training
papers.journal: Proceedings of the Institution of Mechanical Engineers. Part H, Journal of Engineering in Medicine
papers.design: Device design, manufacture and bench validation
papers.n: One manikin neck prototype (bench-tested against motion capture)
papers.finding: The prototype delivered six-degree-of-freedom neck motion with realistic low stiffness and head-angle accuracy within 0.89° RMSE versus optoelectronic motion capture

papers.title: What patients think of alternative response units
papers.design: Scoping review
papers.n: 3 studies across diverse settings
papers.finding: Key experience constructs: convenience of home-based care, avoiding unnecessary ED attendance, perceived competence plus interpersonal communication, reassurance and psychological safety, and perceived longer-term benefit from referral and continuity of care

papers.title: Psychological first aid for paramedic families
papers.design: Qualitative interviews and focus group, reflexive thematic analysis
papers.n: 11 interviews plus one focus group of 5, 6–9 months after training
papers.finding: Four themes: communicating with care and confidence, navigating the 'not normal', creating an open culture, and sustaining support beyond the programme; participants reported better work-to-home transitions and stronger family and peer relationships

papers.title: Supporting bystanders after failed resuscitation
papers.design: Perspective/review
papers.n: Not reported
papers.finding: Unsuccessful resuscitation involvement can cause emotional distress, intrusive memories, guilt and PTSD symptoms; supportive follow-up contact and referral pathways are proposed over formal debriefing

papers.title: Overdrive pacing for refractory pVT prehospital
papers.design: Case report
papers.n: 1 patient
papers.finding: Transcutaneous overdrive pacing was implemented prehospital as rescue for recurrent polymorphic VT after OHCA when transvenous pacing was unavailable

papers.title: Ambulance contamination hotspots: cuffs and sats probes
papers.design: Cross-sectional ATP bioluminescence sampling
papers.n: 23 high-touch sites per vehicle, 1,932 total tests
papers.finding: Pulse oximeter (>1,100 RLU) and blood pressure cuff exceeded the very-high contamination threshold; paramedic hand RLU fell from 349.79 to 34.79 after handwashing

papers.title: EMS alcohol education: limited and patient-focused
papers.design: Qualitative semi-structured interviews
papers.n: 31 EMS clinicians across multiple US certification levels and regions
papers.finding: Existing alcohol-related education described as limited, passive and patient-care focused; participants wanted EMS-specific data, physiological content, personal narratives and interactive delivery plus peer and family support

papers.title: Transport ventilation during CPR feasible in pilot
papers.design: Prospective, time-sequenced exploratory pilot (6 months bag-valve, then mechanical ventilation)
papers.n: 41 adults with OHCA (29 bag-valve, 12 mechanical ventilation)
papers.finding: No significant differences in PCO2, pH or pO2, sustained ROSC or 28-day survival between groups; mechanical ventilation feasible despite implementation challenges

papers.title: Longer on-scene intervals linked to 24-hour mortality
papers.design: Retrospective cohort, ALS dispatch, restricted cubic splines
papers.n: 2,321 Code Red EMS activations, Saraburi Province
papers.finding: On-scene interval of 21-25 minutes was associated with higher odds of 24-hour mortality versus 5 minutes or less (aOR 5.61, 95% CI 1.58-19.97); non-survivors had a longer median on-scene interval (12 vs 9 minutes)

papers.title: Tele-paramedics matched physicians in MCI drill
papers.design: Prospective simulation-based controlled quasi-experimental study within a 7.5-hour MCI exercise
papers.n: 151 simulated patients across 7 treatment tents
papers.finding: Indicated treatments addressed: 51% tele-paramedic vs 57% tele-physician vs 56% on-site physician vs 8% EMT-only (p < 0.001); analgesia addressed in 60%, 59%, 68% and 7% respectively; time to first treatment order did not differ

papers.title: What drives lay community first responders in Denmark
papers.design: Qualitative interpretative phenomenological analysis, semi-structured interviews
papers.n: 10 community first responders without a professional healthcare background
papers.finding: Four themes: a sense of duty, acting under uncertainty as a civilian-turned-responder, navigating relational roles with professionals and peers, and carrying the self into crisis; volunteers driven by moral duty, meaningfulness and community

papers.title: Paramedic training problems vary by placement setting
papers.design: Qualitative phenomenological design, semi-structured interviews, thematic analysis
papers.n: 15 paramedic and student participants, Turkey
papers.finding: 10 sub-themes across 36 codes: station problems were linked to the system itself, emergency department problems to patients and staff attitudes, and high student numbers were seen as harming both education and service delivery

papers.title: Physician burnout dimension linked to self-rated health
papers.design: Cross-sectional study, ordinal regression models, convenience sample
papers.n: 151 prehospital emergency physicians, one Belgrade EMS
papers.finding: Higher emotional exhaustion was associated with less favourable self-rated health (OR per 10-point increase 1.31, 95% CI 1.04-1.64); the association weakened after mutual adjustment (OR 1.30, 95% CI 0.96-1.75); depersonalisation and reduced personal accomplishment showed no clear associations

papers.title: Trauma analgesia safety confirmed across four drug classes
papers.design: Systematic review of RCTs and observational studies
papers.n: 17 studies, 17,115 injured adults over 15 years
papers.finding: All four agent classes (opioids, ketamine, methoxyflurane, paracetamol) showed effectiveness; no drug-attributed serious adverse events except one opioid study, with minor effects like nausea and drowsiness common.

papers.title: Undertriage in trauma linked with higher in-hospital mortality
papers.design: Retrospective statewide cohort with doubly robust causal modelling
papers.n: 59,095 injured adults, 2023 Pennsylvania discharge data
papers.finding: Undertriage rate 53%; adjusted risk ratio for in-hospital mortality 1.19 (95% CI 1.07–1.33); shorter length of stay (-0.29 days); over-60s less likely to be discharged home (aRR 0.95).

papers.title: Prehospital blood linked to arrival hypocalcaemia in trauma
papers.journal: The American Journal of Emergency Medicine
papers.design: Preplanned subanalysis of a prospective multicentre observational study
papers.n: 1,047 EMS-transported trauma patients at 3 US trauma centres
papers.finding: 235 patients hypocalcaemic and 39 hypercalcaemic on arrival, both associated with lower survival; 77 of 136 (56.6%) who received prehospital blood were hypocalcaemic; 5 hypercalcaemic patients had received prehospital calcium, suggesting possible iatrogenic hypercalcaemia.

papers.title: Prehospital SBP ≥180 linked with worse stroke outcomes
papers.journal: Journal of Stroke and Cerebrovascular Diseases
papers.design: Retrospective multicentre cohort
papers.n: 1,106 EMS-transported LVO stroke patients, mean age 79, 60% thrombectomised
papers.finding: SBP ≥180 vs <120 mmHg: adjusted OR 0.43 (95% CI 0.22–0.84) for mRS 0–2 at 90 days; significant in EVT-treated patients, not in non-EVT patients (interaction p=0.007); haemorrhagic complications similar across groups.

papers.title: Central venous access during arrest feasible in simulation
papers.design: Simulation-based feasibility study
papers.n: Repeated simulations with a multidisciplinary team (EMS clinicians plus a physician) in a standard ambulance
papers.finding: Cannulation successful in all simulations via standard sterile technique; left femoral vein identified as the most practical site; main challenges were confined workspace and fixed stretcher height.

papers.title: CT stroke unit model separates diagnosis from transport
papers.design: Conceptual model design informed by a global survey of MSU programmes
papers.n: Not reported (conceptual model, no patient data)
papers.finding: The model separates CT-based diagnosis from treatment and transport; patients are moved to a standard EMS vehicle after CT evaluation, which the authors argue may make MSU deployment feasible in resource-constrained regions.

papers.title: In-flight events uncommon in international air repatriation
papers.design: Retrospective observational cohort with multivariable regression
papers.n: 3,905 international fixed-wing repatriations, single Canadian provider, 2009–2024
papers.finding: In-flight events in 26.7% of transports, major events 3.9%; independent predictors of events were age, orthopaedic/trauma and neoplasm diagnoses, oxygen therapy, invasive ventilation and transport year; acuity increased over time.

papers.title: Fatigue common among US helicopter air ambulance pilots
papers.design: Cross-sectional survey with standardised sleep questionnaires
papers.n: 120 pilots across 21 US HAA operators
papers.finding: 53% reported poor sleep quality; 71% felt fatigue was most prevalent on the return-to-base leg; 69% named flight request volume as the biggest schedule-related contributor; 34% reported nodding off in flight; 87% said sleep inertia affected performance.

papers.title: Flight simulation training: engagement shown, evidence thin
papers.design: Systematic review (CASP appraisal of 7 articles)
papers.n: 7 studies of high-fidelity simulation for critical care paramedics
papers.finding: Learners reported improved expertise, engagement, motivation, responsiveness and mood; evidence was insufficient on self-awareness and on performance of trained crews in the prehospital setting; authors recommend standardised training and assessment.

papers.title: New ambulance nurse induction: four challenges, three fixes
papers.design: Qualitative participatory action research (2020–2024)
papers.n: One Swedish ambulance service organisation (newly employed nurses, supervisors, management)
papers.finding: Four interrelated challenges consolidated; three interventions implemented (restructured theory and practice, prepared clinical supervisors, integrated peer learning); reflection showed theory-practice integration, supervision, leadership and peer learning were interdependent.

papers.title: Resuscitative thoracotomy: no survivors past 10 minutes
papers.design: Prospective national service evaluation (PHOTON, TERN, NaTRIC networks)
papers.n: 116 patients undergoing resuscitative thoracotomy (82 prehospital)
papers.finding: 43.1% achieved ROSC and 6.9% survived to discharge; outcomes were substantially better with cardiac tamponade than exsanguination, and there were no survivors beyond 10 minutes of traumatic cardiac arrest

papers.title: Ultrasound tube confirmation: thin evidence on the road
papers.design: Scoping review (Joanna Briggs Institute framework, PRISMA-ScR)
papers.n: 51 studies from 2,447 records
papers.finding: Only one of 51 included studies evaluated diagnostic performance in adult patients in an out-of-hospital setting; no included study measured patient-oriented outcomes

papers.title: Machine learning predicts good recovery after OHCA
papers.design: Multicentre prospective registry (Korean Hypothermia Network, KORHN-PRO)
papers.n: 1,358 comatose adult OHCA survivors treated with targeted temperature management
papers.finding: The voting-classifier model predicted 6-month neurologically intact survival (29.3% of patients) with AUROC 0.929 and AUPRC 0.850; the top five predictors were prehospital initial rhythm, arrival rhythm, age, PaCO2 and total collapse duration

papers.title: Teen drinking falls, alcohol ambulance call-outs don't
papers.design: Retrospective registry analysis with multivariable regression, stratified by gender and remoteness
papers.n: 25,928 ambulance attendances for adolescent alcohol intoxication (ages 10–19), Victoria 2012–2023
papers.finding: A small but significant monthly decline occurred only among males in major cities (B = −0.01, P < .001); no significant trends for males in regional areas or for females in metropolitan or regional areas

papers.title: AED coverage depends on how responders travel
papers.design: Spatial optimisation modelling (multimodal location set covering and maximal covering problems)
papers.n: 17,842 ambulance dispatch records and 3,569 existing AEDs across 1,161 grid cells in Wuhan
papers.finding: Baseline demand-weighted 4-minute coverage was 85.07% for driving, 68.27% for cycling and 31.55% for walking; universal coverage required 68 additional AEDs under a driving assumption versus 521 under walking

papers.title: Real-time BVM feedback linked to better arrest ventilation
papers.design: Prospective before/after quality assurance study
papers.n: 278 adults with OHCA (148 before / 130 after)
papers.finding: Ventilations in-target for both rate and tidal volume rose from 7.5% to 39.0% with real-time feedback; with ETCO2 monitoring alone only 6.8% met both, and 58.2% of ventilations delivered a lower-than-target tidal volume

papers.title: Women still get less bystander CPR in public
papers.design: Retrospective dual-registry cohort (CARES North Carolina, Pan-Asian RESC Singapore)
papers.n: 6,828 OHCAs in North Carolina and 3,617 in Singapore
papers.finding: Public bystander CPR: 48% of men vs 44% of women in North Carolina (aOR 0.87) and 59% vs 52% in Singapore (aOR 0.78); survival to discharge favoured women in North Carolina (aOR 1.15) but men in Singapore (aOR 0.63)

papers.title: Adrenaline timing not tied to paediatric OHCA survival
papers.design: Retrospective national registry cohort with time-dependent propensity matching (JAAM-OHCA, Japan)
papers.n: 259 children with witnessed OHCA who received adrenaline
papers.finding: No timing window (1–10 through 26–30 minutes after EMS contact) showed an association with one-month survival; risk ratios ranged 0.97–2.94 with confidence intervals crossing 1

papers.title: ECG signs appear minutes before post-ROSC rearrest
papers.design: Retrospective cohort, 2018–2024
papers.n: 1,298 adults with OHCA achieving ROSC
papers.finding: 40.7% of post-ROSC patients rearrested; identification was highest one minute before rearrest (AUROC 0.74) and declined beyond three minutes; rearrest carried lower survival (20.4% vs 43.1%) and favourable neuro outcome (7.8% vs 21.2%)

papers.title: Severe hypertension in pregnancy rarely treated to guideline
papers.design: Retrospective observational cohort (2024 ESO Data Collaborative)
papers.n: 39,546 EMS scene responses for pregnancy beyond 20 weeks
papers.finding: Persistent severe hypertension in 3.1% (1,234/39,546); of those, 6.2% received magnesium only, 1.5% an antihypertensive only, and 0.8% both magnesium and an antihypertensive

papers.title: Few heat-stroke cooling devices suit the prehospital setting
papers.design: Systematic review of commercially available cooling devices
papers.n: 18 commercial cooling devices
papers.finding: Three of 18 devices met the ideal cooling threshold (≥0.155°C/min), two were acceptable (0.078–0.154°C/min), 61% reported no cooling-rate data, and five met the ≤16 kg single-person portability limit

papers.title: AI ECG model excludes ACS after cardiac arrest
papers.design: Single-centre retrospective cohort with temporal validation
papers.n: 400 adults with post-ROSC OHCA (329 development / 71 validation)
papers.finding: The tree labelled 52.0% of development and 45.1% of validation patients 'ACS not likely' with zero missed ACS cases; yield concentrated in non-shockable rhythms (64.8% of non-ACS cases excluded, AUROC 0.824)

papers.title: Ambulance infection control hinges on human factors
papers.design: Modified nominal group technique consensus study
papers.n: 10 experts (infection prevention, paramedicine, governance, education, operations)
papers.finding: Human factors ranked first among determinants of compliance, followed by education and training, physical environment, equipment and consumables, and contaminated equipment management

papers.title: Community paramedicine cut hospital admissions in cluster RCT
papers.design: Cluster-randomised controlled trial with repeated cross-sectional analysis
papers.n: 30 apartment buildings across five Ontario communities
papers.finding: Hospital admission rates were lower in intervention buildings during the 12-month trial (aIRR 0.75) and the following year (aIRR 0.82); primary care visits fell then rose post-trial; ED visits unchanged

papers.title: Simulated EMS care held up at altitude
papers.journal: Scandinavian Journal of Trauma, Resuscitation and Emergency Medicine
papers.design: Assessor-blinded randomised crossover simulation study (physician-staffed crews)
papers.n: 20 non-acclimatised EMS physicians (17 analysed)
papers.finding: Median composite performance 82% at baseline, 74% during acute exposure to 3,450 m, 82% with supplemental oxygen at 4 L/min, and 83% after 20 hours at altitude; overall difference not significant (p=0.082)

papers.title: Swedish bleeding control guidelines scored low on quality
papers.journal: Scandinavian Journal of Trauma, Resuscitation and Emergency Medicine
papers.design: Cross-sectional AGREE II appraisal of regional clinical practice guidelines
papers.n: Guidelines from 15 Swedish healthcare regions
papers.finding: Clarity of presentation scored highest; rigour of development, stakeholder involvement, applicability and editorial independence scored poorly; most guidelines lacked evidence search strategies, evidence links and update procedures

papers.title: Drone AEDs arrived first in two-thirds of arrests
papers.design: Bibliometric analysis, scoping review and policy document analysis
papers.n: 168 studies reviewed; 62 Chinese policy documents analysed
papers.finding: Drone AEDs arrived before ambulances in 67% of cases (median lead time 3 min 14 s); drone blood delivery reduced transport time 61%; modelled networks were cost-effective with OHCA survival gains of 21–46% under model assumptions

papers.title: Facial recognition helped paramedics ID unknown patients
papers.design: Double-blind randomised controlled simulation study
papers.n: 90 firefighter-paramedics (48 experimental / 42 control)
papers.finding: 83.3% of the app group identified the standardised patient vs 21.4% of controls (OR 13.87); secondary outcomes included retrieving key medical information and treatment appropriateness

papers.title: Fewer ultrasound frames preserved remote B-line detection
papers.design: Retrospective deep-learning evaluation of expert-labelled clips
papers.n: 1,844 expert-labelled lung ultrasound clips from 214 patient groups
papers.finding: B-line sensitivity 89.4% with 5 frames vs 90.1% with 32 (paired difference −0.7 points); package size fell 84% (526 to 84 KB) and idealised transfer at 0.1 Mbps fell from 43 to 7 seconds

papers.title: Nursing-home arrests more often shockable, linked to early AED
papers.design: Population-based registry cohort, descriptive plus multivariable logistic regression
papers.n: 2,478 medical-origin OHCAs, Japan, 2016–2024
papers.finding: Initial shockable rhythm: 36.3% in nursing homes vs 7.1% at home (aOR 12.35, 95% CI 8.93–17.24) and 33.4% in other locations; 97.0% of shockable nursing-home cases got an AED shock; one-month favourable neurological survival lowest in nursing homes at 0.8%

papers.title: Bystanders describe heavy emotional toll of doing CPR
papers.design: Qualitative — semi-structured interviews, reflexive thematic analysis
papers.n: 11 bystanders (9 knew the patient), recruited via social media, Scotland
papers.finding: Four themes: emotional impact; managing multiple roles; compelled to help but unprepared; talking to the right person

papers.title: NZ paramedics breached patient rights more often than nurses
papers.journal: Whitireia Journal of Nursing, Health and Social Services
papers.design: Descriptive statistical analysis of published regulatory breach decisions
papers.n: 109 breach decisions (9 paramedics, 100 nurses), NZ, 2014–2024
papers.finding: Per 1,000 practitioners, paramedics were three times more likely than nurses to breach the Code and breached at a higher severity rate; Right 4 was the most prevalent breach in both professions

papers.title: Drone triage feasible but unproven in real MCIs
papers.journal: Scandinavian Journal of Trauma, Resuscitation and Emergency Medicine
papers.design: Scoping review (JBI methodology, PRISMA-ScR), 20 original studies
papers.n: 20 studies — 8 acquisition, 11 decision-support, 1 effectiveness
papers.finding: Remote capture of heart rate, respiratory rate, temperature, SpO2, consciousness and location is feasible; the single randomised comparison showed UAV-assisted triage took ~3.5 min longer with identical accuracy; no validated remote triage standard exists

papers.title: Ambulance CTG streamed to hospital during maternal transfer
papers.design: Prospective feasibility study with staff surveys
papers.n: 68 women with singleton pregnancies beyond 22 weeks, Japan, 2021–2023
papers.finding: All 68 fetal heart-rate records legible, median 91.1% legible recording time; median ambulance time 34.5 min (range 15.0–67.0); no monitoring sessions discontinued for connectivity

papers.title: Lab work targets haemolysis in stored whole blood
papers.design: Animal laboratory study — haemorrhagic shock and transfusion in hamster dorsal window chamber model
papers.n: Adult male Golden Syrian hamsters across stored-blood groups with low, moderate or severe haemolysis
papers.finding: Stored whole-blood haemolysis correlated negatively with haematocrit, microvascular flow and functional capillary density, and positively with organ injury markers and lactate; the scavenger protein cocktail mitigated capillary collapse and tissue injury but caused haemodilution without recovery of haematocrit, pH or lactate to baseline

papers.title: Defining quality in bystander CPR
papers.journal: International Journal of Nursing Studies Advances
papers.design: Modified Delphi consensus study (two survey rounds plus a virtual consensus meeting)
papers.n: 104 panellists registered; 62, 48 and 18 completed rounds 1–3
papers.finding: Consensus (≥75% agreement) on 11 indicators covering chest compression rate, depth and recoil and contextual factors including dispatcher instruction, time from recognition to emergency call and AED use; two composite indicators were created and all criteria scored dichotomously.
